unlisted_practices: AI deployment studies should report who led clinical workflow design, local model adaptation or validation, implementation, frontline training, evaluation, and organizational change, including cross-trained hybrid expertise.
Future meta-research on AI trials should classify outcomes (structural, process, patient-important) and analyse effect magnitudes, not only statistical significance.

Preregister AI deployment studies beyond randomized trials, including prospective cohort, stepped-wedge, interrupted time-series, and before-and-after designs, to distinguish prespecified primary outcomes from post hoc favorable reporting.

Health systems or multicenter consortia should prospectively follow AI deployment efforts using a common protocol recording team composition, leadership type, comparator choice, end-user involvement, governance structure, adoption, fidelity, workflow workarounds, and sustainability.
Embed qualitative interviews or process evaluations alongside quantitative outcomes when evaluating AI deployment.
Use modeling approaches appropriate for sparse outcomes, such as Firth-corrected or rare-events logistic regression, when analyzing rare events in AI deployment literature.

screen.reason: Commentary critiquing the methodology and evidence of a prior study that linked clinical leadership/authorship to AI deployment outcomes.
